synopsis: Accepted narrowly for pieces 02 and 03 as a founder/practitioner account of physical experiment automation and verification. Its contribution is operational: telemetry, replicates, execution provenance, human involvement, and an anecdote connecting simulations to a subsequent experiment. These offer a contrasting case for students designing computational experiments, not validated evidence of superior performance or savings. The supplied September 29 publication date falls within the frozen September 16–October 15 window; dates of the underlying experiments are unspecified. All later substantive claims still require passage citations.
limitations_and_counterevidence: This is a commercially interested founder interview, not an independently replicated study. The supplied account provides no inspectable execution logs, controlled baselines, held-out evaluation results, ablations, detailed hardware/model configurations, or audited cost breakdown supporting its performance anecdotes. The introduction's thousands-per-day framing must be paired with later future scaling language; actual throughput is unestablished. Human choices and handling remain part of the described workflow. The cost comparison concerns an estimate at maximum second-lab throughput, not demonstrated expenditure savings. Other interviews with these founders cannot independently corroborate this account. The automatic transcript is provisional; no audio verification was performed, and uncertain wording has not been repaired. The segment locators below are anchors; explicitly listed adjacent segments are required context.

Supports an attributed operational lesson, not measured improvement in reproducibility.

Opening capability framing requiring counterevidence. Include adjacent s00024, giving s00023–s00024 (106.28–116.38 seconds). This is the host's thousands-of-experiments-per-day description, which must be paired with the future scaling qualification in the next selection.

This qualifies the opening framing and does not establish fully autonomous discovery or a measured speedup.

Cost comparison and its conditional baseline. Include adjacent s01105–s01116, giving s01104–s01116 (2621.98–2652.46 seconds). Preserve the engineer's estimate at maximum second-lab throughput, roughly $30 million annually, alongside the founder's smaller-model, sub-million-dollar comparison. This is an unaudited account without workload, accuracy, training-cost or hardware details, not established savings.

Human direction limits autonomy. Include adjacent s01172–s01180, giving s01171–s01180 (2764.8–2786.26 seconds). Modality selection is described as originally mostly human intuition; claimed LLM contributions are indications and small methodological changes. Preserve these qualifications when discussing agent-designed experiments.

Physical versus computational verification comparison. Include s01270–s01280 (2997.7–3023.34 seconds) for the founder's characterization of coding/math verification and available context, and s01295–s01298 (3054.82–3068.58) for missing context, delayed verification and noise in physical work. Treat this as the founder's conceptual comparison, not proof that all computational outcomes are immediately verifiable.

Commercial interest and evidence independence. Include adjacent s01207–s01216, giving s01206–s01216 (2848.96–2878.36 seconds). The founders discuss custom customer systems and contemplated outcome-based pricing with retained IP. Establishes the commercial perspective of the testimony; it does not itself prove that results are invalid or that supporting records are unavailable elsewhere.
